# Alignment with TRY

[TRY](https://www.try-db.org/) is the plant trait database run by the Max Planck
Institute for Biogeochemistry. It defines traits by name and number, such as trait 14,
*Leaf nitrogen (N) content per leaf dry mass*. This page maps the {{N_TRAITS}} TRY traits
to BERVO. The work is tracked in
[issue #27](https://github.com/bioepic-data/bervo/issues/27) and is done in slices. This
first slice is the map itself. Terms for the traits used by the
[plant-functional-traits](https://github.com/bioepic-data/plant-functional-traits)
schema come next, and further slices follow from the gaps listed here.

## Sources

| Source | Revision | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `try_traits.csv`, attached to issue #27 | 2026-01-29 | The {{N_TRAITS}} TRY traits, as `trait_id` and `trait_name` only. It is byte-identical to `data/try_traits.csv` in plant-functional-traits. |
| [`bioepic-data/plant-functional-traits`](https://github.com/bioepic-data/plant-functional-traits), `src/plant_functional_traits/schema/plant_functional_traits.yaml` | `d083f09` | Which TRY traits the harmonized schema uses, in the `pft_slot` column |

The TRY list has no units, definitions or value types. A term added from it takes those
from the TRY data release documentation or from the literature the trait comes from, not
from the list. TRY cuts trait names at 100 characters, so a few end mid-word; they are
kept as given.

## The map

The map is `src/scripts/try/try_alignment.tsv`, one row per TRY trait:

| Column | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `trait_id`, `trait_name` | as in TRY |
| `group` | the organ or theme, used to plan slices |
| `status` | one of the five below |
| `bervo_id` | the BERVO term, for `match`, `broader` and `related` |
| `pft_slot` | the plant-functional-traits schema slot the trait feeds, if any |
| `note` | why a `related` term is not the same quantity, or another caveat |

| Status | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `match` | A BERVO term is the same quantity. |
| `broader` | A general BERVO term covers the trait, with the organ or status in `contexts`. For example, *Stem nitrogen (N) content per stem dry mass* is `Plant tissue nitrogen content` with `Stem` in `contexts`. |
| `related` | A BERVO term is close but is not the same quantity, such as a reciprocal, a different normalisation, or an EcoSIM parameter defined differently. A term for the TRY trait is still needed. |
| `gap` | BERVO has no term. |
| `species_attribute` | The trait records where a species occurs, its habitat or indicator values, its legal status, its phylogeny or its uses, rather than a property of a plant. These are set aside for a decision on scope, not rejected. |

Groups and the `species_attribute` status were first assigned by rules on the trait name,
then checked by hand. The C, N and C/N rows in `broader` were assigned the same way. Root
contents per unit of soil mass and root microbial biomass were excluded from them, since
neither is the content of a plant tissue. Every `match` and `related` row was assigned
by hand.

## How the alignment is recorded on a term

- A `match` term records the ID in its `Comment` as `TRY trait ID: 14.`, or
  `TRY trait IDs: 3108, 3109.` when several TRY traits are the same quantity.
- A `broader` term records the IDs as `TRY traits mapped here, with the organ or status in
  contexts: 80, 406.`, following the pattern of the AmeriFlux BADM fields mapped to the same
  terms.
- A `match` term takes the TRY trait name as a `Related Synonyms` value, unless the name is
  already its label or is a label or synonym of another term. TRY's own abbreviations,
  such as SLA, LDMC and SSD, go in `Exact Synonyms`.
- TRY has no registered prefix, and its trait pages have no stable URL, so there is no
  `TRY:` cross-reference in `DbXrefs`.

`just try-doc` rebuilds this page, and it fails if the map and the `Comment` sentences
disagree. `tests/test_try_alignment.py` runs it.

## The plant-functional-traits schema

The schema harmonizes TRY, AusTraits and fine-root trait data into one record per taxon.
It is preliminary, so these rows are where the next slice starts, not the limit of it.
Several of its TRY columns are aggregates of more than one TRY trait. Leaf area, for
example, is spread over seven traits that differ in how a compound leaf and its petiole
are counted, so each slot lists every trait it may draw on. The `leaf_mass_per_area`
slot has no row: TRY has no trait of that name, since LMA is the reciprocal of SLA, and
BERVO already has `Leaf mass per area` (`BERVO:0002185`).
